general: Tell me honestly. Do you know where we are going?
I know where we have been. That has to count for something.
We have been walking since before it was light.
And we will be walking after it is dark. That is the arrangement.
If this all ends badly, I want it written down that I said so.
It is written down. You say it every week.
Do you ever think about going home?
Home is wherever the packs are.
That is a very sad thing to be at peace with.
You have been quiet all day.
I was thinking. It happens.
Tell me again why we took this road.
Because you asked, and I said yes. Fool that I am.
I would not have made it this far alone.
Nor I. Do not let it go to your head.
How is that wound of yours holding up?
It has stopped bleeding, which is something.
If we get paid, I am buying the first round.
You said that in the last three towns.
Do you trust the people we met back there?
I trust nobody I cannot outrun.
You carry too much. Give me half.
I can manage. Ask me again on the hill.
One of these days we should stop for a whole week.
A week. Listen to us.
What did you do before all this?
Something quieter. I do not miss it as much as I should.
How much money have we actually got?
{gold} gold, and half of it is spoken for.
So the answer is no, then.
Say we found somewhere decent tomorrow. Would you stop?
Ask me tomorrow. I am too tired to be honest tonight.
Who is leading this, exactly?
{leader} walks in front. That is not quite the same thing.
I dreamed we were still walking.
That is not a dream, that is a memory arriving early.
I had a dream about this place. Do not ask.
You always dream about the wrong things.
One of these days I will dream about the right one and you will owe me an apology.
Do you think anyone is looking for us?
Somebody always is. It is who that changes.
We should agree on what we do if it goes wrong.
We run. That is the plan. It has never let us down.
I have been counting the days.
How many?
I lost count. That is my point.
Nobody warned me the boring parts would be the worst.
Nobody warned me about any of it.
Your boots are finished.
My boots have been finished since spring. They have not been told.
I keep expecting somebody to come and take charge.
That was the job nobody applied for.
What is the first thing you buy, if we ever come out of this rich?
Silence. A whole room of it.
We are getting good at this.
We are getting used to it. Do not confuse the two.
If I go down, do not carry me. Take the pack and go.
I will carry you and complain the entire way.
I have stopped asking what is over the next hill.
Good. The answer has been disappointing four times running.
Say something interesting. Anything.
The word for a group of crows is a murder.
I regret asking.
Are we the good ones in this?
We are the ones still walking. Ask a historian about the rest.
Do you remember the name of that town? The one with the bells?
No. But I remember the bells.
I want one day where nothing at all happens.
You would be unbearable by noon.
We have not talked properly in weeks.
We are talking now.
This is not talking. This is walking with noise.
What would you be doing right now, if none of this had happened?
Something with fewer hills in it.
That is not an answer. That is a complaint with a hat on.
You have not asked me a single question about myself in a month.
I assumed you would say it when you wanted to.
That is either very considerate or very lazy.
Who taught you to fight like that?
Nobody. That is rather the problem.
I have been keeping a list of everything we are owed.
By whom?
That is the weakness in the list, yes.
Do you think we have changed?
You have got quieter and I have got worse. So yes.
If you could take one thing back out of all of it, what would it be?
Ask me something easier. Ask me about the weather.
Nobody out here knows our names.
That has been the single best part of the last year.
We are going to run out of money before we run out of road.
We have been in that state since the day we met. Keep walking.
Watch out for that one. They are pleasant, and pleasant is expensive.
Noted. And if they are simply pleasant?
Then I will have been wrong twice this year.
How do you sleep, out here, with all of it?
Badly, and then all at once.
That is the most honest thing you have said to me.
We should decide now who carries what if we have to run.
You take the money, I take the water. Neither of us takes the tent.
Say we finish this. Say it actually ends. Then what?
Then I find out whether I am any good at ordinary days.
I do not think either of us is doing this for the money any more.
Speak for yourself. I am doing it entirely for the money.
You could at least pretend to think about it before answering.
Every town we pass is somebody's whole life.
And we are two strangers walking through the middle of it. Try to be polite.
There is something I should have told you a while ago.
Then tell me on the road. I would rather hear it moving.
You can see the Tower from here if you stand on the bank.
I have seen it from four countries. It never looks any further away.
Somebody told me the Tower holds the ninety-two dimensions together.
Like the stick through a sandwich. That was the phrase they used.
That is not reassuring and I have thought about it every day since.
Would you go in? The Tower, I mean. If somebody paid.
I would go in. I would not go up.
They say the door opened on its own in ninety-nine.
Two billion people died that night and a door opened. Those are related.
Ninety-two floors of dimensions and somebody has put a department store in it.
There are camping tents in the corridors. I have seen photographs.
If the Tower is a spear, somebody threw it.
And whatever she was aiming at is still down there under all that rock.
The Foundation charges to go past the third floor now.
They charge to go anywhere. It is neutral ground with a till on it.
Do you believe there is a goddess doing the paperwork?
I believe somebody put a bounty on me for a broken window. Call that what you like.
Everything we do is watched by somebody who is bad at justice.
That is the whole century, summarised.
Have you ever seen a judicial ghost?
Once, from a long way off. It walked in a straight line through a wall.
Then let us keep doing nothing worth a straight line.
A god only exists while people believe in them.
Which means the small ones die of being forgotten. That is a horrible way to go.
They say Draghi is a god now, and he is a number.
Every note in your pocket has his name on it. Do the arithmetic.
Do you pray?
I keep my head down. It works out to about the same thing.
If she were killed, the throne would be empty for a few days.
And every ambitious idiot in ninety-two dimensions would start climbing.
You have thought about this in more detail than I am comfortable with.
Two thousand and twelve. Everyone says it like a date.
It is a deadline. That is why they say it like that.
Do you ever think we are living in the last ordinary years?
I think every generation has believed that. Ours has the arithmetic to back it.
Keep under eighty on this stretch. There is a bubble marked at the bend.
I know. I have driven it before. I would like it noted that I know.
What happens if we go into one?
The same day, forever, until somebody drives out of it at speed.
And nobody outside can telephone in to tell us. Wonderful.
There are people who live in the bubbles on purpose.
You cannot die in one unless something hits you fast enough. That is a bargain some people take.
They send pigeons between the bubbles. Actual pigeons.
With memory sticks tied to their legs. It is the only post that works.
Somebody said the bubbles are getting bigger every year.
They are. That is the point of the deadline.
I would not want to be the one who lives the same day forever.
You already are. You simply have worse weather.
Every road in every world is the same road, apparently.
The Encompassing Road. Take the wrong turn off it and you are somewhere else entirely.
If the engine is calibrated right, a turn-off goes to another dimension.
And if it is calibrated wrong you arrive somewhere with no ground. Choose your mechanic.
There is a god of asphalt, they say. He made the first road.
And was the first thing run over on it. Somebody has a sense of humour.
A man built an engine in a camper and made himself rich.
He built it to get away from somebody. That is what I heard.
Do you think the road knows we are on it?
Ask me again after dark and I will give you a different answer.
The archivists stopped a party ahead of us and read out their messages.
They call it making things public. It is reading somebody's post in the road.
The Collective sells water and buys memories.
And every other liquid on the shelf has something in it. Drink from the well.
Nobody has ever seen an Esoteric Heavy Industries factory.
The crates simply appear in the warehouse when nobody is looking. I have asked.
Their goods ignore the loop. Move it slowly and it still does not reset.
Which is why one of their kettles costs more than this vehicle.
The Guild is the richest faction and it achieves nothing.
It is two halves that hate each other holding the same purse.
Vatican City floats eight hundred metres over Rome now.
And it shoots at anything that comes close. Progress, of a kind.
Would you take work from the Foundation?
I would take their money. I would not sign the release.
The truckers keep the bubble towns alive. That is not a small thing.
They are the only faction I have never been lied to by.
The Naguka came up out of a Soviet borehole. That is the actual history.
Somebody drilled too deep and the world got worse. Twice, if you count the oil.
Hurt one Naguka and the whole species knows.
So do not. It is the simplest rule in the world and people keep breaking it.
The Verden lay eggs and speak better than we do.
And they came from a world that threw its technology into a sun on purpose.
Why would anybody give up everything they had built?
Perhaps they found out what it was for. That is the version that frightens me.
Half the goblin hordes worship a Norwegian band.
And the band has become gods, because enough of them believe it. That is how it works now.
Do not separate the words of a spell. Ever.
I know the law. The universe sends the bill and it is not money.
Say it in one breath and joined up, or do not say it.
CamelCase. It is the first thing anybody learns and the last thing anybody respects.
I saw a grimoire eat a notebook once.
Then it was badly written. A bad spell spreads. Burn the book, not the shelf.
Standing on a leyline makes everything stronger and nothing controllable.
Which is why the good mages are the ones who read maps.
Break a leyline and nothing works there for a generation.
Except the divine ones, and they answer to somebody with opinions.
Lava does not burn you any more. It drains you.
Unless it was conjured. Then it does both, out of spite.
Nobody can leave the atmosphere any more.
There is a mill of scrap going round the planet at eight kilometres a second. Nobody is going anywhere.
They are building rockets out of armour and volunteers.
Free of charge, both directions, and nobody comes back. Very generous.
Mexico looks like Africa from orbit now. In one day.
And everybody who lived there is still there. That is the part people skip.
Somebody in New York lost their soul to a bomb that left the buildings standing.
Do not say that word out loud on this road. Not with the Guild in the next valley.
My grandmother remembered before the sky broke.
Mine claimed to. Everybody's grandmother claims to.
What is the least we could live on?
Less than this. We have proved it twice and I do not want a third proof.
Do you ever count what we are owed?
I stopped. The number stopped being funny.
We could take honest work.
We take honest work. It is the pay that is dishonest.
If one of us came into money, would the others hear about it?
You would hear about it. You would hear about it at length.
Who holds the fund tonight?
Whoever sleeps worst. That is how it has always been settled.
We have never agreed on what a fair split is.
We have never had enough at once for it to be a real argument.
Say we get paid properly, once. What is the first thing?
Boots. Then a room. Then boots again for whoever is still complaining.
What would you have made of me, if we had met in a town?
I would have thought you were somebody's problem. I would have been right.
How long have we been doing this now?
Long enough that I do not count it in weeks any more.
Do you ever want to travel with anybody else?
No. That is not sentiment, it is arithmetic. New people get killed.
I would tell you if I was thinking of leaving.
I know. That is why I sleep.
You went ahead without me at the ford.
I did. I have been waiting for you to say so all afternoon.
We have not had a proper argument in a month.
Give it a week. There is one coming and we both know the subject.
If we stopped tomorrow, would you say it had been worth it?
Ask me somewhere warm and I will lie beautifully.
You are the only person who knows all of it.
And I have never once used it against you. Consider that.
Tell me something you have never told anyone.
No.
That is fair. I would have said no as well.
We should decide now who tells the family, if it goes badly.
Neither of us has one. That is why we are out here.
How many kilometres today, honestly?
More than yesterday. Less than we said this morning.
We have walked past four villages without stopping.
Stopping is how we lost the last three days.
The map is wrong about this whole valley.
Every map has been wrong since ninety-two. They are historical documents now.
Which way at the fork?
The one with the traffic. Traffic means somebody thinks it goes somewhere.
I want a road with a name on it.
You want a road with an inn on it. Say what you mean.
We should be somewhere by dark.
We are always somewhere by dark. It is what sort of somewhere that varies.
Do you know where we are, exactly?
I know where we are roughly, and roughly has kept us alive.
There is weather coming off that ridge.
There is. Walk faster and stop admiring it.
We have been going downhill for two hours and I do not trust it.
Downhill is always paid for. Somewhere ahead there is the bill.
What is the worst road you have ever walked?
This one, eventually. Everything becomes the worst road eventually.
The tent has one more season in it. Maybe.
It had one more season three seasons ago. It is a very brave tent.
We are down to the food nobody wanted.
Then somebody is about to discover they wanted it after all.
Whose turn is the second watch?
Mine. It is always mine, because I am the only one who wakes up.
I have mended this strap four times.
Mend it a fifth. We are not buying a strap in this country's prices.
Everything in this pack is either broken or nearly.
Same as everything carrying it.
Do we have anything for a fever?
We have something for a fever, something for a cut, and a great deal of hope.
I would trade the lamp for a dry coat.
You would trade the lamp and then walk into a hole. No.
That family has been ahead of us since the bridge.
Then let them stay ahead. A road with people on it is a road that goes somewhere.
Would you take a passenger?
Depends who is looking for them.
Everybody out here is going somewhere they will not talk about.
Including us. That is why nobody asks.
Do you trust a man who tells you his whole story in ten minutes?
I trust him to be lying. Whether it matters is another question.
Somebody will offer us work in the next town.
Somebody always does. That is not the same as somebody paying.
The last party we met had one fewer than when they set out.
They did not mention it and we did not ask. That is the etiquette.
Nothing has happened for two days and I am uneasy about it.
Enjoy it. Being uneasy about peace is a habit, not a warning.
What do you think about when there is nothing to think about?
Doors. Rooms with doors. It is not interesting but it is honest.
I have started talking to myself.
I know. I have been answering some of it.
Say something. Anything at all.
There is a bird on that post that has been watching us for a kilometre.
Thank you. That was worse than the silence.
Do you think anyone writes any of this down?
Somebody in the Foundation, probably. Badly, and without our names.
One day I will tell all of this properly, in order.
You will tell it out of order, and better, and half of it will be untrue.
Do you want the good news or the arithmetic?
The arithmetic. The good news is always the arithmetic with a hat on.
We have not been paid in full once this year.
We have not finished a job in full once this year. I am not defending them, only counting.
I have worked out what we spend a week.
Do not tell me.
It is more than we earn.
I asked you not to tell me.
If a stranger offered us honest work at honest pay, what would you say?
I would say no, out of habit, and think about it for a month.
We are good at this and nobody knows.
That is the business. Nobody knows any of the good ones.
What would make you turn a job down?
Children in it. That is the whole list and it has never been added to.
The last man who hired us knew our names before we said them.
Then somebody sold him our names. That is a service now.
Do we have a reputation?
We have four, in four countries, and only one of them is accurate.
I have been thinking about doing something else.
Everybody thinks about doing something else. On this road, at this hour, everybody.
What else could you do?
Anything with a roof and a grimorie. I would be terrible and I would be warm.
Say we save enough. What would you buy?
Somewhere with a door I own. That is the entire fantasy.
The Collective would take us on tomorrow.
The Collective takes everybody on tomorrow. It is what happens on the day after that.
I would not work for the archivists.
You would work for the archivists if it was winter and we were hungry. So would I.
Everything we own is on our backs.
Everything we own is on our backs and nobody can take it in the night. There are worse arrangements.
I have started giving the boots names.
That is the second stage. The third is arguing with them.
We should keep a proper record of the routes.
You keep saying that and then we walk instead.
What is the furthest east you have been?
Further than I will admit to on a road with people on it.
Do you know what today is?
It is a walking day. They are all walking days.
It is the solstice.
Then it is a long walking day.
What month is it, honestly?
I know what month it is. I am simply not going to say it out loud, because of the number after it.
Somebody ought to name this road.
It has a name. Everything has a name. Nobody uses them any more, that is all.
Do you think the roads will still be here after?
After? The roads are the one thing that will be here after. Ask the truckers.
Eleven years.
Do not do that. Do not count down out loud.
Everyone talks about the deadline like it is weather.
It is weather. That is exactly what it is, and you cannot argue with weather.
Some of the dimensions are already gone, they say.
Not gone. Emptied. The people came here. That is why the roads are busy.
Where do you think the goblins actually came from?
Downwards. And they have every right to be annoyed about the drilling.
The Verden woman in that market spoke better than I do.
She has spoken it for two years. You have spoken it your whole life. Sit with that.
Do you believe the story about the band?
I believe enough goblins believe it, which is the only part that matters.
I met a man who claimed to have been inside a petrodemon contract.
Then he was lying or he was rich. Which was he?
Rich.
There you are, then.
Everything runs on oil that used to be a lizard with opinions.
Say that again in a town and see what happens to you.
I saw an Anoki phone on a trucker's dash. An actual one.
Then he is somebody. They do not hand those out.
Could you telephone a god on one, do you think?
You could telephone something. Whether you would like the answer is the question.
The banknotes have Tower scrapings in them.
Which is why they do not reset in a bubble. Everything in this century is held together with paint.
Who is actually in charge? Of anything?
Whoever answers when you telephone. And nobody answers.
There are three Americas and none of them are free.
There is one Britannia and it owns a coast of one of them. Do not start.
Was there ever a time when the world was simple?
There was a time when the lies were more consistent. People call that simple.
Do you remember television?
There is still television. It is simply mostly a man reading numbers.
I would like to see the sea from the other side once.
There is no other side any more. Not without a rocket and a bad plan.
A whole cage of scrap going round the planet.
And volunteers queuing up to be fired through it for nothing. People are extraordinary.
Do you ever want to know how it ends?
No. I want to know where we sleep. Those are different sizes of question.
We have walked further this year than most people walk in a life.
And seen the same four things in eleven countries.
Which country was the best?
The one where nobody asked for papers. I have forgotten which one that was.
Which was the worst?
The one we are in tomorrow. It is a good system, this pessimism.
Do you keep anything from the places we pass?
A stone from each. It is stupid and the pack is heavy and I am not stopping.
I have started forgetting the order of it.
Then it has become a life instead of a journey. That is not the worst thing.
Say we are still doing this in ten years.
Then somebody has been very lucky and it is not going to be both of us.
Would you want to be remembered?
I would want somebody to know where I stopped. That is different and it is enough.
Nobody has written our names down anywhere.
The Foundation has. Twice. In the wrong spelling.
What was your first road?
A short one, out of somewhere I do not talk about. Ask me a different question.
We have never had this conversation properly.
We have had it four times. You forget it every time and I let you.
Tell me about the winter before we met.
It was cold and I was alone and I have made it sound better every year since.
Do you think we are friends, or something else?
We are something else. There is not a word and I am not going to invent one on a hill.
I would notice if you were gone.
That is the most romantic thing anybody has said to me in a decade.
You have never asked me for anything.
I have asked you for everything. You have simply never noticed, because you gave it.
If I asked you to turn round now, would you?
Yes. Do not ask, because I would want a reason afterwards and you would not have one.
We should agree on a signal.
We have a signal.
We have four and none of us can remember which is which.
What do we do if we are separated in a town?
The gate we came in by, at dusk, two days running. Then the road.
I do not want to be carried, if it comes to that.
You will be carried and you will complain. That is the arrangement and it is not open.
Nobody out here says thank you enough.
Thank you.
Not to me. Generally.
Generally, thank you.
I am glad it is you.
Do not go soft on a good road. Save it for the mud.
We should have a rule about the last of the water.
There is a rule. Whoever is worst has it, and nobody admits to being worst.
Who is the sensible one, out of the two of us?
Whichever of us is not talking. It changes hourly.
I have been wrong about something for a long time.
About me?
About me. It will keep. But I wanted it said today.
Do you sleep better when I am on watch?
Yes. Do not make anything of it.
What happens to whoever is left?
They keep walking. That is the whole answer and we both knew it before I said it.
I have made a list of everybody we have lost.
Burn it or carry it. Do not read it on the road.
Some days I cannot remember why we started.
For money. Then it became habit. Then it became this. That is most lives.
We could have been ordinary.
We could have been ordinary somewhere that got emptied. Do not romanticise it.
What is the best day you have had out here?
One with nothing in it. A dry road and nobody wanting anything.
Then today is a candidate.
Today is a candidate. Do not tell it.
Everything hurts and I am content. Explain that.
You are tired and safe at the same time. It happens perhaps twice a year.
Do you ever talk to people who are not here?
Every night on the second watch. It is the only thing that keeps me awake.
Somebody is going to ask us for help in the next town.
Somebody always does. Say yes to the small one and no to the interesting one.
I have stopped being able to say no.
Then I will say it for you, and you can be cross with me and grateful later.
We have never once turned round because it was hard.
We have turned round twice because it was stupid. That is a better record.
Have we ever done anything that mattered?
Twice. You were asleep for one of them.
What would you change?
Nothing that is in my hands. Everything that is not.
Sometimes I think we are only walking to stay ahead of thinking.
That is exactly what we are doing. It is a working method.
The next town, I am going to sit down and not stand up for a day.
The next town has a hill in it. I have seen the map.
Everything east of here is somebody else's story.
Then let us go and be a minor character in it for a week.
Do you want to know what I want?
Yes.
A quiet week and somebody else's roof.
That is not a want, that is a shopping list.
We are going to be all right, are we not?
We are going to be all right today. I do not do further than that any more.
Keep talking. It makes the hill shorter.
It does not make the hill shorter. It makes it possible, which is better.
I have run out of things to say.
Then say nothing well. That is a skill and you have never had it.
We have another two hours in us.
We have another two hours in us and then a very honest conversation about the tent.
Tell me it is worth it.
It is worth it.
You said that too quickly.
I have had a long time to practise.
I want it on record that I was here.
You are on record. I am the record. It is not a good one but it is yours.
What do you think about when you walk?
Doors, dinners, and whether the strap will hold. In that order, all day.
Nobody ever writes about the walking.
Nobody ever writes about the waiting either, and that is most of it.
One more ridge and then we stop.
You said that at the last one.
I will keep saying it until one of them is true.
Is there anything you would not tell me?
One thing. And this is not the road for it.
Then tell me on a better road.
There is not going to be a better road. But I will tell you anyway, eventually.
That is the sun going.
Then walk faster and admire it later.
Twelve hours and we have not argued once.
Give it until the tent. The tent is where the arguing lives.
Same time tomorrow?
Same time tomorrow. Same road, worse weather, probably.
Right. Onwards, then.
Onwards. It is the only direction with anything in it.
Are you going to tell me what happened at the ford, or do I guess?
Guess. You are usually kinder than the truth.
What is the plan if neither of us can walk?
Then we are somewhere with a roof, or we are not, and there is no third case.
I would like one day where nobody wants anything from us.
That day exists. It is always the day after tomorrow.
Do you think about what we are walking towards, or only away?
Away. It has been away for a long time now.
Somebody said the roads are getting safer.
Somebody says that in every town, and it is always somebody who does not travel.
We should write down what we are owed and by whom.
You have. Twice. You lost both.
If we found a place, would you stop?
I would stop for a winter. That is as far as I will commit on a hill.
I have been counting the days again.
How many?
I lost count. That is what I keep discovering.
Everything about this year has been slightly wrong.
Everything about the last twelve has. This one is only closer.
Tell me the plan out loud so I can hear how bad it is.
There is no plan. There is a direction and some food.
That is the second time you have said that today.
Then it is the second time it has been true today.
We are going to be fine.
Say that again with something behind it.
We are going to be fine.
Do you want to know what I have decided about all this?
Not on a hill. Tell me when we are sitting down.
battered: Nobody here is in a fit state to fight anything.
Then we do not fight. We sit down and we mend.
Look at us. All three of us, if we are counting.
I would rather not be counted just now.
We are one bad afternoon from being buried in a field.
Then let us have a good afternoon. For once.
Everyone is hurt. Not one of us is pretending otherwise any more.
That is the first honest thing said all day.
If something comes at us now, it takes us.
Then we stop. Here. Whatever it costs us in hours.
Say it. Somebody say it.
We are in a bad way and we need to stop.
Thank you.
Everybody sit down. All of you, now.
And then what?
And then we find out what we have left.
Count the bandages and say the number out loud.
Three. Three, and one of them has been used.
Then nobody takes a risk until the next town.
We cannot take another fight today. Not one.
Then we walk round whatever is next, however far round is.
Look at the state of the three of us.
I would rather not. I have been avoiding it since noon.
Somebody has to say we are in trouble.
We are in trouble.
Thank you. It is easier now it is out.
If anything finds us in the next hour it takes us.
Then we make sure nothing finds us. Off the road, under cover, no fire.
I can walk. I cannot fight, but I can walk.
That is all today asks of you.
Who is worst? Honestly, not bravely.
Not me. And that is all I am going to say about it.
We should have turned back at the bridge.
We should have. It is said. Now bind that arm.
The plan is to stop being hurt. That is the whole plan.
It is a good plan. It has no steps in it, but it is a good plan.
